components.html:
[ 02 · ABOUT ]

Speed with structure

Systems that scale because they were designed to, not because we hoped.

components.name: Blueprint Coordinate Label
components.description: Signature mono drafting callout used as an occasional section marker.

narrative.overview: The portfolio of an engineer who started before AI was the default copilot and now uses it as a power tool — so the interface is built like a precise technical drawing: a true white drafting surface, black ink, a measured grid, hairline rules, and monospace coordinate labels. The system is monochrome by doctrine; the only chroma permitted anywhere is the brand color of the technology logos themselves, rendered full-saturation against the grey field. Motion is engineered, not garnish — a Three.js wireframe field, GSAP scroll choreography, and Framer Motion micro-interactions, each with a reduced-motion fallback.
keyCharacteristics: True-neutral monochrome surface; tech-logo brand color is the sole accent.
Serif display (Playfair) + humanist sans body (Plus Jakarta) + technical mono (JetBrains Mono).
Visible measured grid, hairline rules, mono coordinate/section labels.
Crisp corners, generous negative space, drafting-set restraint.
Motion is engineered (Three.js / GSAP / Framer Motion), never ornamental.

rules.name: The Logos-Are-The-Only-Color Rule
rules.body: Chroma is forbidden on every surface except the technology logo marks. No accent color of our own — not on links, buttons, focus rings, or a single dot. Emphasis comes from weight, size, and contrast within greyscale.

rules.name: The True-Neutral Rule
rules.body: Every grey is chroma 0. No warm paper/cream/sand tint, no cool slate tint. Warm-neutral near-whites are the 2026 AI default and are forbidden.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-For-Machines Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved for things a machine would print: coordinates, counts, status, the animated code line. Never set prose in mono.

rules.name: The One-Serif-Statement Rule
rules.body: Playfair earns its drama by scarcity. One serif statement owns each viewport; supporting text is sans or mono.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces rest flat with a 1px border. A shadow at rest is wrong — shadows are earned by hover/focus and true overlays.

dos: Do keep every surface true-neutral greyscale (chroma 0) and let only the technology logos carry color, at full saturation.
Do pair Playfair Display (serif, headlines only) with Plus Jakarta Sans (body) and JetBrains Mono (technical labels) — three jobs, no overlap.
Do separate surfaces with a 1px hairline and the paper→surface→elevated ramp; reserve shadow for hover/focus and true overlays.
Do treat motion as part of the build: Three.js wireframe atmosphere, GSAP scroll choreography, Framer Motion micro-interactions — each with a prefers-reduced-motion fallback.
Do cap body measure at 65–75ch and hold body/caption text at ≥4.5:1 (Muted Ink #595959 or darker on white).
Do use the mono Blueprint Coordinate Label as a deliberate, occasional system.
donts: Don't introduce any accent color of our own — no blue links, buttons, focus rings, dots, or the old electric #3b82f6. The logos are the only color.
Don't use background-clip:text gradient text or any gradient as decoration.
Don't ship the generic SaaS / purple-gradient template, glassmorphism-by-default, or the hero-metric cliché.
Don't build the crowded dev-portfolio look — no skill bars, percentage meters, badge walls, or busy timelines.
Don't go neon-cyberpunk or corporate stock-photo agency.
Don't tint the neutrals warm or cool; chroma stays at 0.
Don't put a mono coordinate eyebrow above every section, and don't set prose in the serif or in mono.
Don't gate content visibility behind a motion-triggered reveal; animate an already-visible default.
